extracted.intended_audience: inventors, legal practitioners, and historians seeking the statutory rules on monopolies and early patent rights (England, 1623)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the statutory standards from the 1623 Statute of Monopolies governing when monopolies/patents are void or allowed, procedural remedies for injuries, and specific exceptions and exclusions. Useful for understanding historical patent/monopoly legal criteria and procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voidance of monopolies and related grants
rubrics_metrics.description: All monopolies and all commissions, grants, licences, charters, letters patents ... of or for the sole buying, selling, making, working, or using of anything within this realm ... and all proclamations, inhibitions, restraints, warrants of assistance, and all other matters and things whatsoever, any way tending to the instituting, erecting, strengthening, furthering, or countenancing of the same, or any of them, are altogether contrary to the laws of this realm, and so are and shall be utterly void and of none effect, and in no wise to be put in ure or execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies an extensive list of instruments that grant exclusive privileges or dispense with law; declares them contrary to law and void. Includes grants to dispense with statutes or compound penalties, and any warrant to secure such dispensations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication by common law courts only
rubrics_metrics.description: And all monopolies ... and the force and validity of them, and every of them, ought to be, and shall be for ever hereafter examined, heard, tried, and determined, by and according to the common laws of this realm, and not otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disputes about monopolies must be decided by the common law courts (not by prerogative or other extrajudicial mechanisms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incapacity to hold or exercise monopolies
rubrics_metrics.description: And all person and persons, bodies politic and corporate whatsoever, which now are or hereafter shall be, shall stand and be disabled, and uncapable to have, use, exercise, or put in ure any monopoly, or any such commission, grant, license, charter, letters patents, proclamation, inhibition, restraint, warrant of assistance, or other matter or thing tending as aforesaid, or any liberty, power, or faculty grounded or pretended to be grounded upon them, or any of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a statutory disability: no person or corporate body may hold or exercise monopolistic privileges described in the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil remedies and trebled damages for injuries from monopolies
rubrics_metrics.description: If any person ... shall be hindered, grieved, disturbed, or disquieted, or his or their goods or chattels ... seized, attached, distrained, taken, carried away, or detained by occasion or pretext of any monopoly ... that then and in every such case the same person and persons shall and may have his and their remedy for the same at the common law by any action or actions to be grounded upon this statute; ... shall recover three times so much as the damages which he or they sustained ... and double costs:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a statutory cause of action in common law courts and enhanced remedies (treble damages and double costs) for those injured by monopolies or their enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue and procedural limitations on stays and excuses in monopoly suits
rubrics_metrics.description: The same action and actions to be heard and determined in the courts of king's bench, common pleas, and exchequer, or in any of them, ... and in such suits or for the staying or delaying thereof, no essoign, protection, wager of law, aid, prayer, privilege, injunction, or order of restraint, shall be in any wise prayed, granted, admitted, or allowed, nor any more than one imparlance:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the permitted venues (King's Bench, Common Pleas, Exchequer) and restricts procedural devices that could delay or avoid determination (e.g., essoign, wager of law); limits to one adjournment (imparlance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for causing stays or delays by colour of orders or authority
rubrics_metrics.description: If any person or persons shall after notice given that the action depending is grounded upon this statute, cause or procure any action at the common law grounded upon this statute to be stayed or delayed before judgment by colour or means of any order, warrant, power, or authority, ... or after judgment had ... shall cause or procure the execution of or upon any such judgment to be stayed or delayed by colour or means of any order, warrant, power, or authority, ... then the said person and persons so offending shall incur and sustain the pains, penalties, and forfeitures ordained and provided by the statute of provision and praemunire made in the sixteenth year of the reign of king Richard the second.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes severe penalties (praemunire-style pains and forfeitures) on those who improperly obstruct enforcement of monopoly actions by invoking orders or authorities outside the proper court process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception: letters patent for new manufactures to true and first inventor (≤14 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provided also, that any declaration before mentioned shall not extend to any letters patents and grants of privilege for the term of fourteen years or under, hereafter to be made, of the sole working or making of any manner of new manufactures within this realm to the true and first inventor and inventors of such manufactures, which others at the time of making such letters patents and grants shall not use, so as also they be not contrary to the law nor mischievous to the state by raising prices of commodities at home, or hurt of trade, or generally inconvenient:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates the statutory exception recognizing limited-term exclusive rights (patents) to the 'true and first inventor' of a new manufacture for up to 14 years, but conditions them on not being contrary to law or harmful to public welfare (e.g., raising prices, hurting trade).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of the 14-year patent term
rubrics_metrics.description: The same fourteen years to be accounted from the date of the first letters patents or grant of such privilege hereafter to be made,
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that the 14-year exclusive term runs from the date of the first letters patent or grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-prejudice to prior parliamentary grants and acts
rubrics_metrics.description: Provided also, that this act or anything therein contained shall not in any wise extend or be prejudicial to any grant or privilege, power, or authority whatsoever heretofore made, granted, allowed, or confirmed by any act of parliament now in force, so long as the same shall so continue in force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects existing statutory grants/privileges enacted by Parliament from being invalidated by this Act while they remain in force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for warrants/privy seals to justices to compound forfeitures
rubrics_metrics.description: Provided also, that this act shall not extend to any warrant or privy seal made or directed ... to the justices of the courts of the king's bench or common pleas, and barons of the exchequer, justices of assize, justices of oyer and terminer and gaol delivery, justices of the peace, and other justices for the time being, having power to hear and determine offences done against any penal statute, to compound for the forfeitures of any penal statute depending in suit and question before them, or any of them respectively, after plea pleaded by the party defendant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves the historical power of certain judicial officers to compound for forfeitures in penal statutes; these judicial compounding powers are not affected by the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-application to city/borough charters, customs, corporations, companies, and trade societies
rubrics_metrics.description: Provided also, that this act or anything therein contained shall not in any wise extend or be prejudicial unto the city of London, or to any city, borough, or town corporate within this realm, for or concerning any grants, charters, or letters patent to them, or any of them made or granted, or for or concerning any custom or customs used by or within them ... or unto any corporations, companies, or fellowships of any art, trade, occupation, or mystery, or to any companies, or societies of merchants within this realm erected for the maintenance, enlargement, or ordering of any trade or merchandise; but that the same charters, customs, corporations, companies, fellowships, and societies, and their liberties, privileges, powers, and immunities, shall be and continue of such force and effect as they were before the making of this act, and of none other;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carves out long-standing municipal charters, corporate privileges, guilds, companies, customs, and their liberties from the Act's general prohibition on monopolies; preserves pre-existing local and corporate privileges.
